pericarditis.side_effects: Anti-inflammatories can irritate the stomach and kidneys.
pericarditis.followup: Follow-up to confirm resolution and watch for fluid around the heart.
pericarditis.recovery: Most recover fully; it can recur in some.

pad.confirm: Assessed by comparing pulses and blood pressure in the legs and arms.
pad.treatment: Stopping smoking, supervised exercise, and medicines for cholesterol and blood pressure; severe cases may need a procedure. A cold, pale, painful leg is an emergency.
pad.duration: A long-term condition managed over time.
pad.side_effects: Medicines for cholesterol/blood pressure have manageable side effects.
pad.recovery: Symptoms often improve with exercise and risk-factor control.

pancreatitis.confirm: Hospital blood tests (amylase/lipase) and sometimes a scan.
pancreatitis.treatment: Hospital care: fluids into a vein, pain relief, and treating the cause (often gallstones or alcohol). Seek urgent assessment.
pancreatitis.duration: Hospital stay of days; longer if severe.
pancreatitis.side_effects: Severe cases can affect other organs.
pancreatitis.followup: Follow-up addresses the cause (gallbladder surgery, alcohol support).
pancreatitis.recovery: Mild cases recover in days; severe pancreatitis is serious and needs intensive care.

cholecystitis.confirm: An ultrasound of the gallbladder and blood tests.
cholecystitis.treatment: Hospital antibiotics and pain relief, often followed by surgery to remove the gallbladder. Seek urgent assessment.
cholecystitis.duration: Hospital stay of days; surgery may be planned.
cholecystitis.followup: Surgical follow-up; a low-fat diet helps meanwhile.
cholecystitis.recovery: Removing the gallbladder usually cures it; most live normally without one.

cluster_headache.confirm: Recognised from severe one-sided pain around the eye in bouts, with a watering eye or blocked nose.
cluster_headache.treatment: Specific treatments (high-flow oxygen, triptan injections/sprays) and preventers; a doctor or neurologist guides this.
cluster_headache.duration: Attacks last weeks to months in clusters.
cluster_headache.side_effects: Triptans aren't for everyone (e.g. heart disease); discussed with a clinician.
cluster_headache.recovery: Attacks are severe but treatable, and clusters settle between bouts.

gca.confirm: Urgent blood tests and sometimes a temporal-artery biopsy or scan.
gca.treatment: Start steroids urgently on suspicion — do not wait — to protect sight; see a doctor the same day.
gca.duration: Steroids are tapered over many months.
gca.side_effects: Long steroid courses need bone and sugar protection and monitoring.
gca.recovery: Prompt steroids protect vision; delay risks sudden sight loss.

parkinson.confirm: A clinical diagnosis by a neurologist from the movement pattern.
parkinson.treatment: Medicines that boost dopamine, plus physiotherapy and speech/occupational therapy, tailored over time.
parkinson.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
parkinson.side_effects: Parkinson's medicines have effects that are balanced carefully.
parkinson.recovery: Treatment can control symptoms well for a long time.

dementia.confirm: Assessment of memory and thinking, with tests to exclude reversible causes; sudden confusion is different and urgent.
dementia.treatment: Treating reversible contributors, some medicines, and practical and social support for the person and carers.
dementia.duration: A long-term condition; support needs grow over time.
dementia.side_effects: Dementia medicines have modest effects and side effects reviewed by a specialist.
dementia.recovery: While not curable, the right support greatly improves quality of life.

polymyalgia.confirm: Recognised from shoulder/hip stiffness in older adults, with blood tests.
polymyalgia.treatment: A course of steroids usually brings quick relief; a doctor guides tapering.
polymyalgia.duration: Steroids tapered over months to a couple of years.
polymyalgia.side_effects: Long steroid courses need bone/sugar protection and monitoring.
polymyalgia.followup: Regular review; watch for giant cell arteritis symptoms (headache, jaw ache, vision change).
polymyalgia.recovery: Symptoms often improve dramatically with treatment.

scabies.confirm: Recognised from intense itch (worse at night) and a rash, often between the fingers.
scabies.treatment: A treatment cream or lotion applied over the whole body, repeated after a week; treat close contacts and wash bedding/clothes hot.
scabies.duration: Itch can linger 2–4 weeks after successful treatment.
scabies.followup: Re-treat if new spots appear after a few weeks.
scabies.recovery: Fully curable; itch fading over weeks doesn't mean treatment failed.

measles.confirm: Recognised from fever, cough, red eyes and a spreading rash; confirmed by a saliva/blood test. Tell the clinic before visiting.
measles.treatment: Mostly supportive — rest, fluids, fever relief; stay away from others. Seek urgent care for breathing trouble, drowsiness or fits.
measles.followup: Public-health follow-up; check vaccination of contacts.
measles.recovery: Most recover fully; vaccination prevents it and protects others.

lyme.confirm: Recognised from a spreading 'bullseye' rash after a tick bite; blood tests support later stages.
lyme.treatment: A course of antibiotics; see a clinician promptly, especially with the rash.
lyme.recovery: Early treatment usually cures it; untreated it can affect joints, heart or nerves.

bipolar.confirm: A mental-health assessment of mood highs and lows over time.
bipolar.treatment: Mood-stabilising medication and talking therapy, coordinated by a mental-health service; crisis support when needed.
bipolar.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
bipolar.followup: Regular psychiatric review and relapse planning.
bipolar.recovery: Many people live full lives with the right treatment and support.

psychosis.treatment: Antipsychotic medication and psychological and social support; early-intervention services help. Seek urgent help, especially if there is risk to self or others.
psychosis.duration: Early treatment over months; longer-term support varies.
psychosis.side_effects: Antipsychotics have side effects monitored by the team.
psychosis.recovery: Early treatment improves outcomes; many recover well.

eating_disorder.confirm: A compassionate assessment of eating, thoughts and physical health.
eating_disorder.treatment: Specialist eating-disorder support combining therapy, nutrition and medical monitoring. Reaching out early helps.
eating_disorder.followup: Regular review of physical health and progress.
eating_disorder.recovery: Recovery is possible; you deserve support. In the US, the National Alliance for Eating Disorders helpline can help.

hiv_acute.confirm: A blood test; a short flu-like illness weeks after possible exposure is the clue.
hiv_acute.treatment: See a clinician for testing; modern HIV treatment is highly effective and started early. Emergency preventive medicine (PEP) only helps within 72 hours of exposure.
hiv_acute.duration: Testing is quick; treatment is lifelong and effective.
hiv_acute.followup: Sexual-health clinic follow-up and partner notification support.
hiv_acute.recovery: With treatment, people live long, healthy lives and can become non-infectious.

scarlet_fever.confirm: Recognised from a sandpaper rash, sore throat and 'strawberry tongue'.
scarlet_fever.treatment: A course of antibiotics; see a clinician. Keep away from others until 24 hours of antibiotics.
scarlet_fever.duration: Improves within a week on antibiotics.
scarlet_fever.followup: Re-check if not improving or if joint pains or dark urine follow.
scarlet_fever.recovery: Fully treatable; antibiotics also prevent rare complications.

ca_warn_breast.confirm: This is a 'worth getting checked' flag, not a diagnosis. For a breast change (lump, skin or nipple change), a clinician arranges a breast examination and usually a mammogram and/or ultrasound.
ca_warn_breast.treatment: There is no treatment until a cause is found. The step is assessment: most such changes turn out not to be cancer, but checking early is what matters.
ca_warn_breast.duration: Assessment is usually arranged within weeks (sooner for urgent-referral features).
ca_warn_breast.followup: Attend the referral and any tests; chase results if you don't hear back.
ca_warn_breast.recovery: Finding a cause early gives the best options whatever it turns out to be.

laryngitis.confirm: Recognised from a hoarse voice and sore throat, usually with a cold.
laryngitis.treatment: Rest the voice, fluids, steam and warm drinks; it is usually viral so antibiotics don't help.
laryngitis.followup: See a clinician if hoarseness lasts over 3 weeks.
laryngitis.recovery: Voice returns fully; persistent hoarseness should be checked.

lactose.confirm: Recognised from bloating, wind and loose stools after milk; a trial of avoiding lactose helps confirm.
lactose.treatment: Cut back lactose, use lactose-free products, or take lactase enzyme drops; a dietitian can help keep calcium up.
lactose.duration: Symptoms ease within days of reducing lactose.
lactose.followup: Review diet to stay balanced in calcium and vitamin D.
lactose.recovery: Well managed by diet; many tolerate small amounts.

anal_fissure.confirm: Recognised from sharp pain and bright blood on wiping after a hard stool.
anal_fissure.treatment: Soften stools (fibre, fluids), warm baths, and a soothing/relaxing ointment; most heal without surgery.
anal_fissure.duration: Many heal within a few weeks.
anal_fissure.side_effects: Ointments can cause headache or local irritation.
anal_fissure.followup: See a clinician if not healing in 6 weeks or bleeding changes.
anal_fissure.recovery: Usually heals fully with stool-softening measures.

ovarian_cyst.confirm: Often found on an ultrasound; many cause no symptoms.
ovarian_cyst.treatment: Most simple cysts need only watchful waiting with a repeat scan; some need removal. Sudden severe one-sided pain with faintness is an emergency (possible twist or rupture).
ovarian_cyst.duration: Many resolve on their own over weeks to months.
ovarian_cyst.recovery: Most are harmless and settle without treatment.

dysmenorrhea.confirm: Recognised from cramping pain with periods.
dysmenorrhea.treatment: Anti-inflammatory pain relief, heat, and gentle exercise; hormonal contraception can reduce period pain.
dysmenorrhea.duration: Eases as the period ends; preventers work cycle to cycle.
dysmenorrhea.followup: See a clinician if pain is severe, worsening, or new (to check for causes like endometriosis).
dysmenorrhea.recovery: Usually well controlled with simple measures.

trigeminal_neuralgia.confirm: Recognised from brief, electric-shock face pains triggered by touch, chewing or wind.
trigeminal_neuralgia.treatment: Specific nerve medicines (such as carbamazepine), not ordinary painkillers; a neurologist may consider procedures.
trigeminal_neuralgia.duration: Often comes in bouts with remissions.
trigeminal_neuralgia.side_effects: Nerve medicines cause drowsiness and need monitoring.
trigeminal_neuralgia.recovery: Most get good control with the right medicine.

fibromyalgia.confirm: A clinical diagnosis of widespread pain, poor sleep and fatigue, after excluding other causes.
fibromyalgia.treatment: Graded exercise, sleep and stress management, pacing, and sometimes medicines for pain or sleep.
fibromyalgia.duration: A long-term condition managed over time.
fibromyalgia.side_effects: Any medicines' effects are reviewed with the prescriber.
fibromyalgia.followup: Regular review to adjust the plan.
fibromyalgia.recovery: Symptoms often improve with an active, paced self-management approach.

lupus.confirm: Blood tests and the pattern of symptoms; assessed by a rheumatologist.
lupus.treatment: Medicines that calm the immune system (such as hydroxychloroquine and, in flares, steroids), plus sun protection.
lupus.duration: A long-term condition with flares and remissions.
lupus.recovery: Well-managed lupus allows a full life; flares are treated as they come.

sjogrens.confirm: Blood tests and tests of tear and saliva production.
sjogrens.treatment: Artificial tears, saliva substitutes and good dental care; sometimes immune-calming medicines.
sjogrens.duration: A long-term condition managed with daily care.
sjogrens.recovery: Symptoms are managed well with daily measures.

raynauds.confirm: Recognised from fingers/toes turning white then blue then red in the cold.
raynauds.treatment: Keep warm (gloves, layers), avoid smoking; severe cases may need medicines that open blood vessels. New, one-sided or ulcerating changes need review.
raynauds.duration: A long-term tendency managed by staying warm.
raynauds.side_effects: Vessel-opening medicines can cause headache or flushing.
raynauds.followup: Review if attacks are severe or skin breaks down.
raynauds.recovery: Most manage well with warmth; secondary causes need treatment.

myasthenia.confirm: Nerve/muscle tests and antibody blood tests by a neurologist.
myasthenia.treatment: Medicines that improve nerve-muscle signalling and immune-calming treatment. Sudden breathing or swallowing weakness is an emergency.
myasthenia.duration: A long-term condition; treatment is tailored.
myasthenia.side_effects: Medicines need monitoring; some drugs worsen it and are avoided.
myasthenia.recovery: Many achieve good control; watch for breathing/swallowing changes.

menopause.confirm: Usually recognised from the pattern of periods and symptoms around midlife.
menopause.treatment: Lifestyle measures, and hormone therapy (HRT) or non-hormonal options discussed with a clinician based on your health.
menopause.side_effects: HRT's benefits and risks are weighed individually.
menopause.followup: Review to adjust treatment and check bone and heart health.
menopause.recovery: Symptoms are very treatable; many feel much better with the right plan.

pcos.confirm: Based on the pattern (irregular periods, excess hair/acne) with blood tests and sometimes an ultrasound.
pcos.treatment: Weight and lifestyle measures, hormonal treatment to regulate periods, and specific help for fertility, hair or sugar as needed.
pcos.duration: A long-term condition managed over time.
pcos.side_effects: Hormonal and other medicines have individual side effects.
pcos.followup: Regular review of periods, sugar and heart-risk factors.
pcos.recovery: Symptoms are manageable, and fertility is often achievable with help.

endometriosis.confirm: Suspected from painful periods and pelvic pain; often confirmed by a specialist, sometimes with keyhole surgery.
endometriosis.treatment: Pain relief, hormonal treatment to quiet the tissue, and sometimes surgery; fertility support if needed.
endometriosis.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
endometriosis.side_effects: Hormonal treatments have individual side effects.
endometriosis.followup: Gynaecology review to tune the plan.
endometriosis.recovery: Symptoms can be well controlled; care is tailored to your goals.

mastitis.confirm: Recognised from a red, painful, hot area of breast with flu-like feelings, often when breastfeeding.
mastitis.treatment: Keep milk flowing (feed/express), rest, fluids and pain relief; antibiotics if not improving in 12–24h or unwell. Seek care if a tense lump or abscess forms.
mastitis.duration: Often improves within a day or two of good drainage/antibiotics.
mastitis.followup: Re-check if a lump persists after the infection settles.
mastitis.recovery: Most settles quickly; breastfeeding can usually continue.

cushings.confirm: Blood, urine or saliva cortisol tests and scans, guided by an endocrinologist.
cushings.treatment: Treating the cause (often stopping a steroid cause, or surgery for a gland/tumour cause).
cushings.duration: Depends on the cause; recovery over months.
cushings.side_effects: Treatment and steroid adjustments need careful monitoring.
cushings.recovery: Many features reverse once the cause is treated.

bleeding_disorder.confirm: Blood tests of clotting and platelets.
bleeding_disorder.treatment: Depends on the cause — from stopping a contributing drug to specific clotting treatments; avoid aspirin/NSAIDs until assessed.
bleeding_disorder.side_effects: Treatments are specific to the disorder.
bleeding_disorder.recovery: Many causes are very manageable once identified.

menorrhagia.confirm: Assessed with blood tests (for anaemia) and sometimes a scan.
menorrhagia.treatment: Options include anti-inflammatory and tranexamic acid tablets during periods, hormonal treatments (including the hormonal coil), and procedures if needed.
menorrhagia.side_effects: Each option has its own side effects, discussed with a clinician.
menorrhagia.followup: Review for anaemia and treatment response.
menorrhagia.recovery: Bleeding is usually reduced well with treatment.

ectopic_beats.confirm: Often recognised from occasional 'skipped' or extra beats; an ECG or monitor can confirm.
ectopic_beats.treatment: Usually no treatment needed; cut caffeine, alcohol and stress. Seek review if they come with fainting, chest pain or breathlessness.
ectopic_beats.followup: Review if frequent or with worrying symptoms.
ectopic_beats.recovery: Usually harmless in a healthy heart.

vasovagal.confirm: Recognised from a simple faint with warning (hot, dizzy, tunnel vision), often on standing, pain or emotion.
vasovagal.treatment: Lie down and raise the legs at the first warning; stay hydrated; rise slowly. Review if faints are frequent, without warning, or with chest pain/palpitations.
vasovagal.recovery: Simple faints are common and benign when the pattern is typical.

coldsore.confirm: Recognised from a tingling then blistering sore on the lip.
coldsore.treatment: Antiviral cream at the first tingle can shorten it; it heals on its own. Avoid kissing/sharing while active, especially around newborns.
coldsore.side_effects: Creams may irritate; antiviral tablets for frequent cases.
coldsore.followup: See a clinician if very frequent, severe, or near the eye.
coldsore.recovery: Heals fully; the virus stays dormant and can recur.

b12_deficiency.confirm: A blood test for B12 and folate.
b12_deficiency.treatment: B12 by injection or tablets (and folate if low), plus addressing the cause (diet or absorption).
b12_deficiency.duration: Symptoms improve over weeks to months.
b12_deficiency.side_effects: Injections sting briefly; otherwise well tolerated.
b12_deficiency.followup: Repeat bloods to confirm response; some need lifelong treatment.
b12_deficiency.recovery: Tiredness and nerve symptoms usually improve with treatment.

malnutrition.confirm: Assessed from weight loss, poor intake, and blood tests.
malnutrition.treatment: Build up nourishment gradually with help from a dietitian; treat underlying causes; refeed carefully under supervision if severe.
malnutrition.side_effects: Rapid refeeding can be dangerous and is monitored.
malnutrition.recovery: Nutrition and strength usually recover with support.

failure_to_thrive.confirm: Recognised from an infant not gaining weight along their growth curve; assessed by the child's clinician.
failure_to_thrive.treatment: Feeding support and treating any underlying cause, guided by a paediatric team and dietitian.
failure_to_thrive.duration: Recovery over weeks to months with support.
failure_to_thrive.recovery: Most catch up with the right feeding and care.

scurvy.confirm: Recognised from bleeding gums, bruising and tiredness with very low vitamin C intake; a blood test confirms.
scurvy.treatment: Vitamin C replacement and a balanced diet with fruit and vegetables.
scurvy.duration: Symptoms improve within days to weeks.
scurvy.recovery: Recovery is rapid and complete with vitamin C.

weight_health.confirm: A supportive look at eating, activity and overall health — not a judgement.
weight_health.treatment: Realistic, kind changes to food and movement, with support; a clinician or dietitian can help set healthy, sustainable goals.
weight_health.followup: Regular check-ins on goals and wellbeing.
weight_health.recovery: Small sustainable steps work best; you deserve support, not shame.

laceration.confirm: Assessed for depth, bleeding, nerve/tendon involvement and contamination.
laceration.treatment: Press firmly to stop bleeding and clean the wound; deep, gaping, or dirty wounds (or those on the face/hands) may need closure, antibiotics or a tetanus booster — see a clinician. Heavy bleeding that won't stop is an emergency.
laceration.side_effects: Infection risk; watch for spreading redness.
laceration.followup: Wound/stitch check and removal if needed.
laceration.recovery: Most cuts heal well with cleaning and, if needed, closure.

genital_injury.confirm: Assessed gently for bleeding, bruising, and trouble passing urine.
genital_injury.treatment: Seek same-day care for significant bleeding, swelling, or trouble urinating; ice and support help meanwhile. Sudden severe testicle pain is an emergency.
genital_injury.followup: Review if pain, swelling or urinary trouble persists.
genital_injury.recovery: Most minor injuries heal well; prompt care protects function.

dental.confirm: Assessed by a dentist; an X-ray may be needed.
dental.treatment: See a dentist; meanwhile pain relief and avoiding very hot/cold helps. Facial swelling with fever or trouble swallowing/breathing is an emergency.
dental.followup: Dental follow-up and treatment of the cause.
dental.recovery: Most dental problems are very treatable once seen.

urinary_incontinence.confirm: Assessed from the pattern; a urine test rules out infection; a bladder diary helps.
urinary_incontinence.treatment: Pelvic-floor exercises, bladder training, fluid/caffeine adjustments, and sometimes medicines or specialist referral.
urinary_incontinence.side_effects: Any medicines' effects are reviewed with the prescriber.
urinary_incontinence.followup: Review progress; refer if not improving.
urinary_incontinence.recovery: Many improve a lot with pelvic-floor work and simple changes.

neck_strain.confirm: Recognised from muscular neck pain after posture, sleep or minor strain.
neck_strain.treatment: Keep gently moving, heat, posture breaks, and simple pain relief; most settles without tests. Numbness/weakness in the arms or after a significant injury needs review.
neck_strain.side_effects: Pain relievers have the usual cautions.
neck_strain.followup: Review if not improving or with arm symptoms.
neck_strain.recovery: Most neck strain resolves with gentle movement.

breast_pain_cond.confirm: Assessed from the pattern (often cyclical) and an examination.
breast_pain_cond.treatment: Reassurance, a supportive bra, and simple pain relief; cyclical pain often eases. A new lump, skin change or one-sided persistent pain should be checked.
breast_pain_cond.duration: Cyclical pain varies with the cycle.
breast_pain_cond.followup: Examination and, if needed, imaging for focal changes.
breast_pain_cond.recovery: Most breast pain is benign and settles.

nail_hair.confirm: Assessed by looking at the nails/scalp; sometimes a sample is taken.
nail_hair.treatment: Depends on the cause (fungal, inflammatory, deficiency); treatments range from creams to tablets to addressing a deficiency.
nail_hair.duration: Nails and hair grow slowly, so change takes months.
nail_hair.recovery: Many nail and hair problems improve with the right, patient treatment.

insect_sting.confirm: Recognised from local pain, redness and swelling after a sting.
insect_sting.treatment: Remove the sting if visible, clean, cool and use antihistamine/pain relief. Throat/tongue swelling, wheeze or faintness is anaphylaxis — call emergency services.
insect_sting.duration: Local reactions settle over hours to days.
insect_sting.followup: Watch for spreading infection over following days.
insect_sting.recovery: Most stings settle quickly; know the anaphylaxis warning signs.

child_unsettled.confirm: A careful look for a cause (hunger, wind, temperature, illness) and for danger signs.
child_unsettled.treatment: Comfort measures and feeding/winding; seek care for a high fever, poor feeding, fewer wet nappies, a rash that doesn't fade, breathing trouble, or a floppy/very drowsy child.
child_unsettled.followup: Re-check if not settling or danger signs appear.
child_unsettled.recovery: Most unsettled spells are benign, but danger signs always need prompt care.

non_healing_wound.confirm: Assessed for cause (circulation, diabetes, pressure, infection); swabs or blood tests may be needed.
non_healing_wound.treatment: Good wound care, treating the cause, and specialist/tissue-viability input; a sore that won't heal over weeks should always be checked.
non_healing_wound.duration: Healing can take weeks to months.
non_healing_wound.recovery: Most heal with the cause addressed; a persistent non-healing sore needs a proper check.

erectile_dysfunction.confirm: Assessed from the history and a check of heart-risk factors, hormones and medicines (it can be an early heart-risk sign).
erectile_dysfunction.treatment: Lifestyle changes, reviewing medicines, treating causes, and medicines such as tablets that improve blood flow.
erectile_dysfunction.side_effects: ED tablets aren't for everyone (e.g. certain heart medicines); discussed with a clinician.
erectile_dysfunction.recovery: Often very treatable once the cause is addressed.

thrush.confirm: Recognised from itch and thick white discharge; a swab if unclear or recurrent.
thrush.treatment: Antifungal cream or a tablet; avoid irritants. Recurrent thrush should be reviewed.
thrush.followup: Review if frequent or not improving.

bv.confirm: Recognised from a thin grey discharge with a fishy smell; a swab or pH test can confirm.
bv.treatment: A short course of specific antibiotics (tablets or gel); avoid douching and harsh soaps.
bv.side_effects: Antibiotics can upset the stomach; avoid alcohol with some.
bv.recovery: Treats well; recurrence is common and retreatable.

sti_cervicitis.treatment: Specific antibiotics for the infection found, plus testing and treating partners; a sexual-health clinic can do this confidentially and free in many places.
sti_cervicitis.duration: Many infections clear with one course.
sti_cervicitis.followup: A test of cure for some infections; partner notification.
sti_cervicitis.recovery: Most STIs are curable or very manageable; testing protects you and others.

late_period.confirm: Consider pregnancy first (a test), then stress, weight change, illness or hormonal causes.
late_period.treatment: A pregnancy test; if negative and periods stay irregular, a clinician can look for a cause.
late_period.duration: Often a one-off; review if it persists.
late_period.followup: See a clinician if periods stay irregular or stop.
late_period.recovery: Usually benign once pregnancy is excluded; persistent change deserves a check.

self_harm_support.confirm: This is support, not a diagnosis — you reached out, and that matters.
self_harm_support.treatment: Reach out to someone you trust or a crisis line; a clinician or therapist can help with what's underneath. In the US/Canada you can call or text 988.
self_harm_support.duration: Support is ongoing and at your pace.
self_harm_support.followup: A safety plan and regular support help.
self_harm_support.recovery: Things can get better with support; you don't have to manage this alone.

disordered_eating.confirm: A gentle, non-judgemental look at eating patterns and feelings.
disordered_eating.treatment: Talking to a clinician or an eating-disorder service early; support combines therapy and, where needed, nutrition and medical care.
disordered_eating.recovery: Recovery is possible; in the US the National Alliance for Eating Disorders helpline can help.

dissociation_cond.confirm: Recognised from feeling detached, unreal or 'not here', often linked to stress or trauma.
dissociation_cond.treatment: Grounding techniques, reducing stress, and talking therapy; a mental-health service can help, especially if it follows trauma.
dissociation_cond.duration: Episodes often ease with grounding and support.
dissociation_cond.followup: Therapy review if it persists or disrupts life.
dissociation_cond.recovery: Usually improves with support and skills; it's a common stress response.

gingivitis.confirm: Recognised from red, swollen gums that bleed when brushing.
gingivitis.treatment: Thorough but gentle brushing and daily flossing, and a dental/hygienist clean; it reverses with good gum care.
gingivitis.duration: Improves within 1–2 weeks of good care.
gingivitis.recovery: Fully reversible early; untreated it can progress to gum disease.

multiple_sclerosis.confirm: A neurologist assesses the pattern, with an MRI scan and sometimes a lumbar puncture.
multiple_sclerosis.treatment: Treating relapses (often steroids) and, where MS is confirmed, long-term medicines that reduce attacks, plus physiotherapy and symptom care.
multiple_sclerosis.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
multiple_sclerosis.side_effects: Disease-modifying medicines need monitoring; discuss with the specialist.
multiple_sclerosis.recovery: Many people live full lives; early specialist care helps protect function.

encephalitis.confirm: Urgent hospital assessment — brain imaging, a lumbar puncture and blood tests.
encephalitis.treatment: Hospital antiviral or other treatment and intensive support, started urgently. Call your local emergency number now.
encephalitis.duration: Hospital stay of days to weeks; recovery over months.
encephalitis.side_effects: Treatments and intensive care carry risks.
encephalitis.followup: Neurology follow-up and rehabilitation for any after-effects.
encephalitis.recovery: Early treatment improves outcomes; recovery varies.

peripheral_neuropathy.confirm: Blood tests (including sugar and B12) and an examination; sometimes nerve tests.
peripheral_neuropathy.treatment: Treating the cause (e.g. sugar control, B12), and medicines for nerve pain if needed.
peripheral_neuropathy.duration: Depends on the cause; nerves recover slowly.
peripheral_neuropathy.followup: Review of the cause and symptom control.
peripheral_neuropathy.recovery: Often stabilises or improves once the cause is treated.

essential_tremor.confirm: A clinical assessment of when the tremor happens.
essential_tremor.treatment: Often none is needed; if it affects daily life, certain medicines can reduce it.
essential_tremor.side_effects: Tremor medicines have individual side effects.
essential_tremor.followup: Review if it worsens or affects daily tasks.
essential_tremor.recovery: Usually not dangerous and often manageable.

labyrinthitis.confirm: Recognised from the story and an examination of eye movements and balance.
labyrinthitis.treatment: Rest, fluids, and short-term medicines for the spinning/nausea; balance exercises help recovery.
labyrinthitis.duration: Worst for a few days; settles over 2–6 weeks.
labyrinthitis.followup: Review if not improving or hearing is affected.
labyrinthitis.recovery: Most recover fully; balance exercises speed it up.

menieres.treatment: Low-salt diet, medicines to reduce attacks, and treatments for acute vertigo; some need specialist procedures.
menieres.duration: A long-term condition with attacks and quiet spells.
menieres.recovery: Attacks are managed well in most; hearing can change over time.

restless_legs_syndrome.confirm: A clinical diagnosis; blood tests check iron.
restless_legs_syndrome.treatment: Iron if low, lifestyle measures (caffeine, alcohol), and specific medicines if severe.
restless_legs_syndrome.side_effects: Restless-legs medicines have individual side effects.
restless_legs_syndrome.recovery: Often improves a lot once iron and triggers are addressed.

pneumothorax.confirm: A chest X-ray (sometimes a CT) confirms it.
pneumothorax.treatment: Small ones may just be watched; larger ones need the air drained in hospital.
pneumothorax.duration: Hospital stay varies; healing over days to weeks.
pneumothorax.side_effects: Drain procedures carry risks; it can recur.
pneumothorax.followup: Follow-up X-ray; avoid flying/diving until cleared.
pneumothorax.recovery: Most recover fully; some need surgery to prevent recurrence.

pertussis.confirm: Recognised from the cough pattern; a swab or blood test can confirm.
pertussis.treatment: Antibiotics (most useful early) and keeping away from babies; rest and fluids.
pertussis.duration: Cough can linger for weeks ('100-day cough').
pertussis.followup: Public-health follow-up; protect and vaccinate contacts.
pertussis.recovery: Most adults recover fully; vaccination protects babies.

epiglottitis.confirm: Assessed urgently in hospital by specialists who protect the airway first.
epiglottitis.treatment: Emergency airway care, antibiotics and intensive monitoring. Call your local emergency number now.
epiglottitis.side_effects: Significant illness; airway procedures carry risks.
epiglottitis.recovery: With prompt airway care, recovery is usual.

sleep_apnea.confirm: A sleep study (home or in a lab).
sleep_apnea.treatment: Weight and lifestyle measures and often a CPAP breathing device at night; a dental device for milder cases.
sleep_apnea.duration: A long-term condition, well controlled with treatment.
sleep_apnea.side_effects: CPAP takes getting used to; support helps.
sleep_apnea.recovery: Energy, mood and heart risk improve a lot with treatment.

svt.confirm: An ECG during an episode, or a heart monitor, confirms it.
svt.treatment: Simple techniques (bearing down, cold water) can stop an attack; some need medicines or a curative procedure (ablation).
svt.duration: Attacks come and go; ablation can be a long-term fix.
svt.side_effects: Rhythm medicines have individual side effects.
svt.followup: Cardiology review to decide on long-term treatment.
svt.recovery: Very manageable; ablation cures many cases.

costochondritis.confirm: A clinical diagnosis once heart and lung causes are considered.
costochondritis.treatment: Anti-inflammatory pain relief, heat, and avoiding aggravating activity.
costochondritis.duration: Usually settles over a few weeks.
costochondritis.followup: Review if not improving or red flags appear.

postural_hypotension.confirm: Checking blood pressure lying and standing.
postural_hypotension.treatment: Stand slowly, keep hydrated, review medicines; some need added measures.
postural_hypotension.duration: Often improves once the cause is addressed.
postural_hypotension.recovery: Usually well controlled with simple measures.

otitis_externa.treatment: Prescription ear drops and keeping the ear dry; painkillers for comfort.
otitis_externa.followup: Review if not improving or recurring.
otitis_externa.recovery: Clears well with treatment; keep ears dry to prevent it.

quinsy.confirm: Examined by a clinician/ENT; sometimes a scan.
quinsy.treatment: Draining the abscess and antibiotics, usually in hospital.
quinsy.duration: Improves quickly once drained; antibiotics for about a week.
quinsy.followup: ENT follow-up; recurrent cases may need tonsil removal.

tinnitus.confirm: A hearing test and examination; sometimes a scan for one-sided tinnitus.
tinnitus.treatment: Treating any cause, protecting hearing, and sound-therapy or support for bother; no single cure.
tinnitus.duration: Often eases or becomes less noticeable over time.
tinnitus.recovery: Many people habituate and are much less bothered over time.

sudden_hearing_loss.confirm: Urgent hearing tests and ENT assessment.
sudden_hearing_loss.treatment: Often steroids, started as early as possible; treat any cause found.
sudden_hearing_loss.duration: Treatment is urgent; recovery over weeks.
sudden_hearing_loss.side_effects: Steroids have side effects reviewed by the clinician.
sudden_hearing_loss.recovery: Early treatment improves the chance of recovering hearing.

glue_ear.confirm: Examining the ears and a hearing test.
glue_ear.treatment: Often watchful waiting for a few months; some children need small grommets (ear tubes).
glue_ear.recovery: Most children recover fully; hearing returns when fluid clears.

inguinal_hernia.confirm: Usually recognised on examination; sometimes an ultrasound.
inguinal_hernia.treatment: Many are watched; a repair (often keyhole) is offered if it's growing, painful, or at risk. A trapped hernia is emergency surgery.
inguinal_hernia.duration: Elective repair is planned; recovery over weeks.
inguinal_hernia.followup: Surgical review; return urgently for trapped-hernia signs.

bowel_obstruction.confirm: Hospital examination, blood tests and imaging (X-ray/CT).
bowel_obstruction.treatment: Hospital care: rest the bowel (nothing by mouth, a tube, fluids into a vein); some need surgery.
bowel_obstruction.duration: Hospital stay of days; longer if surgery is needed.
bowel_obstruction.recovery: Many settle with rest; surgery is needed for some causes.

ibd.confirm: Stool tests, blood tests and usually a camera test (colonoscopy) with biopsies.
ibd.treatment: Medicines that calm inflammation, specialist diet support, and sometimes surgery; tailored by a gastroenterologist.
ibd.duration: A long-term condition with flares and remissions.
ibd.recovery: Well-managed IBD allows a full life; flares are treated as they come.

ckd.confirm: Blood tests (kidney function) and a urine test; sometimes a scan.
ckd.treatment: Controlling blood pressure, sugar and diet, and protecting the kidneys with specific medicines; advanced cases see a kidney specialist.
ckd.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
ckd.side_effects: Medicines are monitored with blood tests.
ckd.recovery: Progression is often slowed a lot with good control.

epididymitis.confirm: Examination and urine tests; sometimes an ultrasound to exclude torsion.
epididymitis.treatment: Antibiotics, pain relief, rest and support; STI testing where relevant.
epididymitis.duration: Pain eases over days; swelling can take weeks.
epididymitis.followup: Review if not improving; treat partners if an STI.

overactive_bladder.confirm: A bladder diary and a urine test to exclude infection.
overactive_bladder.treatment: Bladder training, cutting caffeine, pelvic-floor exercises, and medicines if needed.
overactive_bladder.side_effects: Bladder medicines can cause dry mouth/constipation.
overactive_bladder.followup: Review progress; refer if not improving.

scrotal_swelling.treatment: Often just reassurance and monitoring; some are treated if large, uncomfortable, or affecting fertility.
scrotal_swelling.side_effects: Any procedure carries the usual risks.

fibroids.treatment: Options range from medicines that reduce bleeding to procedures or surgery, depending on size and symptoms.
fibroids.duration: A long-term condition; fibroids often shrink after menopause.

pelvic_organ_prolapse.treatment: Pelvic-floor physiotherapy, a vaginal pessary, or surgery depending on severity and your wishes.
pelvic_organ_prolapse.recovery: Symptoms usually improve a lot with treatment.

ovarian_torsion.treatment: Emergency keyhole surgery to untwist and save the ovary.
ovarian_torsion.duration: Surgery is immediate; recovery over a couple of weeks.
ovarian_torsion.recovery: The ovary is usually saved if treated quickly.

preeclampsia.confirm: Maternity assessment of blood pressure, urine protein and blood tests, with baby monitoring.
preeclampsia.treatment: Close monitoring, blood-pressure treatment, and timing delivery when needed — the definitive treatment is giving birth. Hospital care.
preeclampsia.duration: Resolves after delivery; monitored closely before and after.
preeclampsia.side_effects: Blood-pressure medicines are chosen for pregnancy safety.
preeclampsia.followup: Maternity follow-up; blood pressure is checked after birth too.
preeclampsia.recovery: Most recover fully after delivery with good monitoring.

gestational_diabetes.treatment: Diet and activity advice, blood-sugar monitoring, and medicine (sometimes insulin) if needed; extra baby monitoring.
gestational_diabetes.duration: Usually resolves after birth; raises future diabetes risk.
gestational_diabetes.side_effects: Insulin/medicine is managed by the team.
gestational_diabetes.followup: Postnatal sugar check and future-risk advice.
gestational_diabetes.recovery: Most pregnancies go well with good control.

psoriasis.treatment: Moisturisers and prescription creams first; light therapy or tablets/injections for more severe disease.
psoriasis.duration: A long-term condition with flares and quiet spells.
psoriasis.followup: Dermatology review for stubborn cases; watch for joint symptoms.
psoriasis.recovery: Well controlled in most with the right treatment.

rosacea.confirm: Recognised by its appearance and triggers.
rosacea.treatment: Trigger avoidance, gentle skincare and sun protection, plus prescription creams or antibiotics.
rosacea.recovery: Redness and bumps usually improve with treatment.

fungal_nail.confirm: A nail clipping can confirm the fungus.
fungal_nail.treatment: Antifungal nail paint for mild cases, or tablets for more; treatment is long.
fungal_nail.duration: Nails grow slowly, so cure takes 6–12 months.

warts.treatment: Over-the-counter salicylic acid or freezing; many resolve untreated.
warts.duration: Can take weeks to months to clear.
warts.followup: See a clinician if unsure of the diagnosis.
warts.recovery: Harmless and usually clears in time.

hand_foot_mouth.treatment: Supportive care — fluids, pain/fever relief; it is viral so antibiotics don't help.
hand_foot_mouth.followup: Re-check if not drinking or very unwell.

cataracts.confirm: An eye examination by an optician or ophthalmologist.
cataracts.treatment: A short, very effective operation to replace the cloudy lens, when vision affects daily life.
cataracts.duration: Surgery is quick; vision improves within weeks.

macular_degeneration.confirm: An eye examination and retinal scans.
macular_degeneration.treatment: Monitoring and lifestyle measures for the common 'dry' type; eye injections can help the 'wet' type if caught early.
macular_degeneration.duration: A long-term condition; early treatment protects sight.
macular_degeneration.followup: Regular eye follow-up; use an Amsler grid at home.
macular_degeneration.recovery: Early treatment gives the best chance of preserving vision.

stye.treatment: Warm compresses; avoid squeezing. A clinician can help if it won't settle.
stye.followup: See a clinician if it grows or recurs.

corneal_abrasion.confirm: An eye examination, often with a dye to show the scratch.
corneal_abrasion.treatment: Lubricating or antibiotic drops; most heal in a day or two. Don't wear contact lenses until healed.

subconjunctival_hemorrhage.confirm: Recognised by appearance; blood pressure may be checked.
subconjunctival_hemorrhage.treatment: No treatment needed; it clears like a bruise.
subconjunctival_hemorrhage.followup: See a clinician if it recurs or you're on blood thinners.

bursitis.confirm: A clinical diagnosis; fluid may be drawn if infection is suspected.
bursitis.treatment: Rest, ice, padding, and anti-inflammatory pain relief; a clinician can drain or inject stubborn cases.
bursitis.followup: Review if not improving or if infected.

frozen_shoulder.confirm: A clinical diagnosis from the stiffness pattern.
frozen_shoulder.treatment: Physiotherapy, pain relief, and sometimes a steroid injection; it recovers in stages.
frozen_shoulder.duration: Can take months to a couple of years.
frozen_shoulder.recovery: Most regain good movement over time.

ankylosing_spondylitis.confirm: Blood tests and imaging (X-ray/MRI) assessed by rheumatology.
ankylosing_spondylitis.treatment: Regular exercise and physiotherapy, anti-inflammatories, and specialist medicines for more active disease.
ankylosing_spondylitis.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
ankylosing_spondylitis.recovery: Staying active keeps the spine mobile; treatment controls symptoms well.

osteoporosis.confirm: A bone-density (DEXA) scan and blood tests.
osteoporosis.treatment: Calcium and vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, and bone-strengthening medicines; treat any cause.
osteoporosis.duration: A long-term condition managed over years.
osteoporosis.side_effects: Bone medicines have specific instructions and side effects.
osteoporosis.followup: Review bone density and fracture risk.
osteoporosis.recovery: Treatment substantially lowers future fracture risk.

tennis_elbow.confirm: A clinical diagnosis from the tender spot and grip pain.
tennis_elbow.treatment: Relative rest, a brace, pain relief and physiotherapy; stubborn cases have other options.
tennis_elbow.duration: Usually improves over weeks to months.
tennis_elbow.recovery: Most recover fully with load management.

ocd.confirm: A mental-health assessment of the thoughts and rituals.
ocd.treatment: Talking therapy (CBT with exposure and response prevention) and, for some, medication.
ocd.duration: Therapy runs over weeks to months.
ocd.side_effects: Any medication's effects are reviewed with the prescriber.
ocd.recovery: Many improve a great deal with the right therapy.

postnatal_depression.confirm: A supportive assessment by your GP, midwife or health visitor.
postnatal_depression.treatment: Support, talking therapy, and medication where needed (options are compatible with breastfeeding).
postnatal_depression.duration: Improves over weeks to months with support.
postnatal_depression.side_effects: Any medication is chosen with feeding in mind.
postnatal_depression.followup: Regular review; involve people you trust.
postnatal_depression.recovery: Most recover fully with support — you don't have to manage alone.

chickenpox.treatment: Supportive care — cooling lotions, antihistamines for itch, fluids and fever relief; antivirals for some at-risk people.
chickenpox.duration: Usually 1–2 weeks; contagious until spots crust over.
chickenpox.followup: Re-check if very unwell or spots look infected.
chickenpox.recovery: Most recover fully; vaccination is available in some places.

mumps.confirm: Recognised from the swelling; a saliva/blood test can confirm.
mumps.treatment: Supportive care — rest, fluids, pain/fever relief; stay away from others.
mumps.followup: Public-health follow-up; check vaccination of contacts.
mumps.recovery: Most recover fully; vaccination prevents it.

chemical_ingestion.confirm: Hospital assessment; the product and amount guide treatment, so bring the container.
chemical_ingestion.treatment: Emergency care; some chemicals have specific treatments. Do not induce vomiting. In the US and Canada call Poison Control 1-800-222-1222; elsewhere call your local poison centre or emergency number.
chemical_ingestion.side_effects: Varies with the chemical and treatment.
chemical_ingestion.followup: Follow-up for any throat or stomach injury.
chemical_ingestion.recovery: Prompt poison-centre advice greatly improves outcomes.

poison_ingestion.confirm: Hospital/Poison-Control assessment; identifying the substance guides treatment.
poison_ingestion.treatment: Emergency care, antidotes for some poisons, and supportive treatment. In the US and Canada call Poison Control 1-800-222-1222; elsewhere call your local poison centre or emergency number.
poison_ingestion.side_effects: Varies with the substance and antidote.
poison_ingestion.followup: Follow-up as advised; some poisons act with delay.
poison_ingestion.recovery: Early poison-centre advice is often life-saving.

alcohol_poisoning.confirm: Recognised from the story and level of responsiveness.
alcohol_poisoning.treatment: Emergency hospital care: monitoring, fluids, and protecting the airway. Call your local emergency number now.
alcohol_poisoning.followup: Support for alcohol use where wanted.
alcohol_poisoning.recovery: Most recover with prompt care; it can be fatal if ignored.

dental_trauma.confirm: A dentist assesses the tooth and may X-ray it.
dental_trauma.treatment: Re-implanting or splinting a knocked-out tooth (best within an hour), or repairing a chip/filling.
dental_trauma.duration: Prompt for trauma; repairs are quick.
dental_trauma.recovery: A quickly re-implanted tooth can often be saved.

child_limb_problem.confirm: Examination, sometimes an X-ray or blood tests/ultrasound.
child_limb_problem.treatment: Depends on the cause — from rest for a minor strain to urgent treatment for infection or fracture.
child_limb_problem.followup: Review until walking/using the limb normally.
child_limb_problem.recovery: Most causes do well when found and treated early.

orbital_eye.confirm: Urgent eye/ENT assessment, often with a scan.
orbital_eye.treatment: Depends on the cause — steroids for optic neuritis, or urgent antibiotics (sometimes surgery) for orbital infection.
orbital_eye.duration: Treatment is urgent; recovery over weeks.
orbital_eye.side_effects: Treatments carry risks reviewed by the specialist.

bradycardia_cond.confirm: An ECG, and sometimes a heart monitor, to check the rhythm.
bradycardia_cond.treatment: Reviewing medicines that slow the heart, treating any cause, and sometimes a pacemaker.
bradycardia_cond.recovery: Often very treatable once the cause is found.

chemical_burn.confirm: Assessed by the depth and the chemical involved.
chemical_burn.treatment: Prolonged irrigation first, then wound/eye care; some chemicals need specific treatment.
chemical_burn.duration: Healing over days to weeks depending on depth.
chemical_burn.recovery: Early, thorough rinsing greatly reduces damage.

electric_injury.confirm: Assessment of the heart (ECG) and for entry/exit burns.
electric_injury.treatment: Monitoring the heart rhythm and treating burns; most minor household shocks need a check and reassurance.
electric_injury.duration: Monitoring for hours; burns heal over weeks.
electric_injury.followup: Follow-up for burns or rhythm concerns.
electric_injury.recovery: Most recover fully; the main risks are rhythm problems and deep burns.

near_drowning.confirm: Assessment of breathing and oxygen, sometimes a chest X-ray.
near_drowning.treatment: Oxygen and observation; more support if the lungs are affected.
near_drowning.duration: Observation for several hours to a day.
near_drowning.followup: Follow-up if the lungs were affected.
near_drowning.recovery: Most recover fully; observation catches delayed breathing problems.

hyperglycemia.confirm: A blood sugar and ketone check.
hyperglycemia.treatment: Follow your sick-day rules, fluids, and insulin adjustment as advised; DKA needs emergency hospital care.
hyperglycemia.side_effects: Insulin changes are guided by your team.
hyperglycemia.recovery: Usually settles with prompt management; learn the DKA warning signs.

hypoxia.confirm: Oxygen measurement and assessment of breathing; a chest X-ray or blood tests may follow.
hypoxia.treatment: Oxygen and treating the cause in hospital. Call your local emergency number for severe breathlessness or blue lips.
hypoxia.recovery: Depends on the cause; low oxygen always needs prompt assessment.

missed_dialysis_cond.confirm: Assessment of fluid, potassium and kidney bloods.
missed_dialysis_cond.treatment: Rescheduling dialysis urgently; emergency treatment if potassium or fluid is dangerous.
missed_dialysis_cond.recovery: Usually manageable if dealt with promptly.

priapism.confirm: Urgent urology assessment; a blood sample from the penis guides treatment.
priapism.treatment: Draining blood and medicines to reverse it; some need a procedure. Time matters.
priapism.followup: Urology follow-up to find a cause.
priapism.recovery: Treated quickly, outcomes are good; delay risks lasting problems.

paraphimosis.treatment: Reducing the foreskin (sometimes after local measures or a small procedure); circumcision may be advised later.

omphalitis.confirm: Urgent assessment of the baby, with blood tests.
omphalitis.treatment: Hospital antibiotics into a vein; babies are watched closely.
omphalitis.recovery: Early treatment gives a full recovery.

gangrene.confirm: Urgent surgical assessment, blood tests and scans.
gangrene.treatment: Emergency care: antibiotics, restoring blood flow, and removing dead tissue; sometimes amputation.
gangrene.duration: Hospital stay and recovery over weeks.
gangrene.side_effects: Major surgery with possible tissue loss.
gangrene.recovery: Outcome depends on how fast treatment starts.

exertional_syncope_cond.confirm: Heart tests — an ECG, sometimes an echocardiogram and monitoring.
exertional_syncope_cond.treatment: Depends on the cause; avoid strenuous exertion until assessed.
exertional_syncope_cond.recovery: Many causes are treatable once found.

gambling_disorder.confirm: A supportive conversation about the impact and any linked low mood or anxiety.
gambling_disorder.treatment: Talking therapy (CBT), support groups, and practical money safeguards; treat any depression/anxiety.
gambling_disorder.duration: Recovery is a journey with support.
gambling_disorder.recovery: Many people regain control with the right help.

tuberculosis.confirm: A chest X-ray and sputum tests; a skin or blood test may be used.
tuberculosis.treatment: A combination of antibiotics taken for about 6 months — finishing the full course is what cures it and stops spread.
tuberculosis.duration: Months of treatment; most feel better within weeks.
tuberculosis.side_effects: Medicines can affect the liver and need monitoring.
tuberculosis.followup: Regular review and support to complete treatment; close contacts are checked.
tuberculosis.recovery: Curable when treatment is completed fully.

rsv_bronchiolitis.confirm: A clinical check of breathing and oxygen.
rsv_bronchiolitis.treatment: Mostly supportive — small frequent feeds, keeping airways clear; some babies need oxygen or help feeding in hospital.
rsv_bronchiolitis.duration: Worst around days 3-5, easing over 1-2 weeks.
rsv_bronchiolitis.followup: Review if breathing or feeding worsens.

norovirus.confirm: Usually recognised from the pattern; no test needed.
norovirus.treatment: Fluids in small frequent sips, rest; oral rehydration salts help. Antidiarrhoeals are generally avoided.
norovirus.followup: Seek care if you can't keep fluids down or show dehydration.

head_lice.confirm: Finding live lice on wet-combing confirms it.
head_lice.treatment: Wet-combing every few days, or a pharmacy lotion repeated as directed; treat the same day as household contacts who also have them.

malaria.confirm: An urgent blood test (repeated if first is negative).
malaria.treatment: Antimalarial medicines; severe cases are treated in hospital.
malaria.duration: Treated over days; severe disease needs intensive care.
malaria.recovery: Treated early, most recover fully; delay is dangerous.

dengue.confirm: A blood test and monitoring, especially of platelets.
dengue.treatment: Supportive care — fluids and paracetamol; watch for warning signs. Avoid NSAIDs/aspirin.
dengue.duration: Fever 2-7 days; warning phase as fever falls.
dengue.followup: Close review during the warning window.
dengue.recovery: Most recover fully with careful monitoring.

typhoid.treatment: A course of antibiotics; some need hospital care.
typhoid.followup: Follow-up to confirm clearance; household hygiene advice.

rubella.confirm: Diagnosis is clinical, confirmed by a blood test; pregnancy is checked.
rubella.treatment: Supportive care — rest and fluids; there is no specific antiviral.
rubella.duration: Rash clears in a few days.
rubella.followup: Public-health notification; pregnant contacts are advised.
rubella.recovery: Full recovery; prevented by MMR vaccination.

androgenetic_alopecia.confirm: A clinical look at the pattern; bloods if another cause is suspected.
androgenetic_alopecia.treatment: Options discussed with a clinician (e.g. topical minoxidil); no treatment is also a valid choice.
androgenetic_alopecia.duration: Any treatment is ongoing; effects take months.
androgenetic_alopecia.side_effects: Topical treatments can irritate the scalp.
androgenetic_alopecia.recovery: A normal part of ageing for many; treatments can slow it for some.

alopecia_areata.confirm: A clinical examination; sometimes blood tests.
alopecia_areata.treatment: Options include steroid creams or injections; many patches regrow on their own.
alopecia_areata.side_effects: Steroid treatments have local side effects.
alopecia_areata.recovery: Often regrows, though it can recur.

telogen_effluvium.confirm: A history of a trigger 2-4 months earlier; bloods if prolonged.
telogen_effluvium.treatment: No specific treatment needed — address the trigger, eat well; be gentle with the hair.
telogen_effluvium.followup: Review if it lasts beyond 6 months.
telogen_effluvium.recovery: Hair density usually returns to normal.

sleep_disorder.confirm: A sleep history; sometimes a sleep study or specialist review.
sleep_disorder.treatment: Depends on the cause — sleep hygiene, a dental night guard for grinding, or sleep-clinic treatment for narcolepsy/REM behaviour disorder.
sleep_disorder.followup: GP then sleep clinic if needed.
sleep_disorder.recovery: Many sleep disorders improve with the right diagnosis.

alcohol_use_disorder.confirm: A supportive conversation about your drinking and any linked low mood or anxiety.
alcohol_use_disorder.treatment: Structured support, counselling, and sometimes medication; medically supervised withdrawal if you drink heavily daily.
alcohol_use_disorder.duration: Recovery is a journey with support.
alcohol_use_disorder.recovery: Many people cut down or stop with the right help.

breastfeeding_support.confirm: A feeding assessment by a midwife, health visitor or lactation specialist.
breastfeeding_support.treatment: Positioning and latch help, feeding support, treating any thrush or mastitis; formula top-ups if needed — fed is best.
breastfeeding_support.duration: Usually improves within days of good support.
breastfeeding_support.recovery: Most feeding problems resolve with help.

postnatal_wound_infection.confirm: A look at the wound and your temperature; sometimes a swab.
postnatal_wound_infection.treatment: Antibiotics and wound care; occasionally the wound needs draining.

post_dates_pregnancy.confirm: Midwife checks of you and the baby (movements, sometimes a scan/monitoring).
post_dates_pregnancy.treatment: Monitoring, a membrane sweep, and planned induction if needed.

benign_skin_lesion.confirm: A clinical look; a dermatologist confirms anything uncertain.
benign_skin_lesion.treatment: Usually none; removal is possible if it bothers you or to confirm the diagnosis.
benign_skin_lesion.recovery: Benign lesions are harmless; the key is watching for change.

developmental_concern.confirm: A developmental review by a GP, health visitor or paediatrician.
developmental_concern.treatment: Depends on findings — speech and language therapy, early-years support, physiotherapy, or reassurance and monitoring.
developmental_concern.recovery: Early support improves outcomes; many concerns resolve or are well supported.

enuresis.confirm: A GP review; a urine test if infection or diabetes is possible.
enuresis.treatment: Reassurance, fluid timing, a bedwetting alarm, sometimes desmopressin; treat any constipation.
enuresis.recovery: Most children become dry with time and support.

catheter_problem.confirm: A check of the catheter and bladder; sometimes a bladder scan.
catheter_problem.treatment: Flushing or changing the catheter by a nurse; treat any infection.
catheter_problem.recovery: Resolves once the catheter drains again.

occupational_exposure.confirm: A GP review with an occupational history; targeted tests (e.g. blood lead) as indicated.
occupational_exposure.treatment: Removing the exposure, specific treatment if a level is high, and workplace controls.
occupational_exposure.recovery: Outcomes are good when exposure is identified and stopped.

contraception_concern.confirm: A clinical check, sometimes an examination or scan to confirm placement.
contraception_concern.treatment: Reassurance, repositioning or replacing a coil, or switching method as you prefer.

acute_urinary_retention.confirm: A bladder scan and examination; blood tests for kidney function.
acute_urinary_retention.treatment: Draining the bladder with a catheter for relief, then finding and treating the cause (prostate, medication, infection).
acute_urinary_retention.duration: Relief is immediate once drained; follow-up over weeks.
acute_urinary_retention.recovery: Good once the cause is treated.

melena_gi_bleed.confirm: Assessment of your pulse and blood pressure, blood tests, and usually a camera test (endoscopy) to find the source.
melena_gi_bleed.treatment: Fluids/transfusion if needed and treatment of the cause (e.g. an ulcer) at endoscopy; stopping any contributing medicines.
melena_gi_bleed.duration: Urgent care over hours to days.
melena_gi_bleed.recovery: Good when the bleeding source is found and treated early.

raised_icp_infant.confirm: Urgent assessment of the baby, often with blood tests, a scan and sometimes a lumbar puncture.
raised_icp_infant.treatment: Depends on the cause — antibiotics for infection, and measures to relieve pressure; babies are watched closely in hospital.
raised_icp_infant.recovery: Best when treated early — do not wait.

perianal_lump_derm.confirm: A clinician looks at the area; an abscess is diagnosed by examination.
perianal_lump_derm.treatment: Warm salt-water (sitz) baths, keeping the area clean and dry; a clinician may drain an abscess (a small procedure) and prescribe antibiotics if infection is spreading. A pilonidal sinus that keeps coming back can need minor surgery.
perianal_lump_derm.duration: Simple cases ease over days; an abscess settles after drainage.
perianal_lump_derm.side_effects: Drainage is done with numbing; minor soreness after.
perianal_lump_derm.followup: See a clinician if it grows, keeps returning, or you develop fever.
perianal_lump_derm.recovery: Good — most resolve fully; recurrent pilonidal disease may need referral.
